title: The Aesthetics of Comparativeness in Islam Observed
core_idea: The article investigates how an interdisciplinary comparative methodology—drawing on anthropology, ethnography, sociology, and literature—is employed in Islam Observed to trace the formation of Islam in Morocco and Indonesia, with particular attention to aesthetic codes and cultural poetics that illuminate regional variations in religious practice and to the literary dimension of the comparative approach.
tldr: Examines how comparative, interdisciplinary methods and the notion of aesthetic codes in Islam Observed illuminate diverse Islamic practices across Morocco and Indonesia and critically engages the literary aspects of that comparative approach.
